description: The publication abstract documents SUMO simulation of urban delivery robots and a mathematical drone-delivery model. It compares one-parcel aerial trips, multi-parcel terrestrial trips and mixed fleets across economic, environmental and social criteria. Drones are faster and robots cheaper or less environmentally costly within the reported scenarios. The geographic case and executable are unknown, and these conclusions do not establish universal fleet performance. The source authors provide the native description and file descriptors through Zenodo. Only metadata was inspected; no measurements, archives, source code or document bodies were retrieved. Public access and the deposit document licence do not establish executable access, software reuse rights or operating costs. Coverage remains bounded to the named experiments, with other geographic and temporal fields unknown. Related project resources may overlap; common project membership does not establish identical simulation inputs or results.
